summary: Iteration 7 security-hardening verification. Wrote 58 new pytest cases in test_security_hardening.py covering all four hardening buckets (SEC-001 dev-login gate + seed admin-only; SEC-002 role/project scoping on /mrf/{id}, /po/{id}, /invoice*, /audit, /billing/items, /users email redaction, /export/*, /po/{id}/grns, /grns; SEC-003 /po/{id}/received purchase/billing/admin only; SEC-004 formula-injection prefix + 5MB upload cap + .xlsx/.xlsm allowlist on both /import/vendors and /import/mrf). All 58 new tests PASS. Additionally patched prior test fixtures (test_project_team.py, test_mrf_po_workflow.py, test_grn_and_import.py, test_invoice_variance.py) so their unauthenticated POST /api/seed calls now use an admin bearer token (required after SEC-001) — this was a test-only fix, not a product change. Full regression: 147/147 passed (58 new + 89 prior).
critical_code_review_comments: SEC-002: _check_po_access allows any site_engineer who created *any* linked MRF; consider also allowing PM/SE on the project team so approved MRFs remain viewable by requester's project peers if needed (spec-dependent).
SEC-002: /api/invoice/{id} does 403 before 404 for non-authorized roles — this is correct (avoids existence oracle) but confirm it is the intended contract.

SEC-004: MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES=5MB is enforced only after the whole body has been read into memory via `await file.read()`; for extreme uploads consider Content-Length pre-check to fail-fast before buffering.

SEC-004: extension allowlist is filename-based only — an .xlsx-named file that is not a valid zip is caught later by openpyxl (400 path), which is fine, but MIME-sniff could be added defense-in-depth.
server.py is 1973 lines — still worth splitting into routers/modules (unchanged from prior iterations).

_safe_cell is applied to string cells only; numeric-first values that begin with '-' (e.g., negative numbers rendered as strings) already covered because they're non-string here; keep an eye if PO totals ever get stringified.
